I-04.hee1: With light, you cannot tell apart things finer than about half its wavelength. That is why the semiconductor world kept searching for "shorter light."

I-05.name: Perceptron
I-05.hee1: The first "learning machine" got smarter just by correcting itself a little each time it made a mistake.

I-06.name: Segregation
I-06.hee1: Sea ice has much less salt than the seawater around it. When it freezes, the salt is pushed out into the remaining water

I-07.name: How the electric arc works
I-07.hee1: The hissing sound of an arc turned out to be carbon reacting with oxygen in the air.

I-08.name: Program
I-08.hee1: Without rebuilding the machine, you can make it do a different job just by changing its instructions (the program).

I-09.name: Defining units by constants of nature
I-09.hee1: One kilogram is no longer a lump in a vault; it is set by a "constant" that is the same anywhere in the universe.

I-10.name: Logarithms
I-10.hee1: A table of numbers that turns multiplication into addition

I-11.name: Creating accuracy without a reference
I-11.hee1: The flattest plate can be made without an even flatter plate. You just need three.

I-12.name: Three primary colors of light
I-12.hee1: Look at a screen with a magnifying glass, and even the white parts are just tiny red, green and blue dots glowing.

I-13.name: Separation of design and manufacturing
I-13.hee1: The brain chip of a smartphone is often designed by one company and made in another company's factory.

I-14.name: Standards
I-14.hee1: A USB cable fits no matter where you bought it, because many companies follow the same rules

I-15.name: Patents and licensing
I-15.hee1: A patent doesn't hide an invention; it is a promise of protection in exchange for making it public.

I-16.name: Supply chain
I-16.hee1: One smartphone contains materials taken from many different places around the world.

I-17.name: CFCs and ozone depletion
I-17.hee1: Because countries around the world kept their promise and stopped using CFCs, the ozone layer is slowly starting to recover.

I-18.name: Coandă effect
I-18.hee1: When you bring the back of a spoon near tap water, the water is pulled toward the spoon. That is the Coandă effect.

I-19.name: Diesel exhaust, air pollution, and countermeasures
I-19.hee1: Today's diesel buses have a filter that catches soot, and the collected soot is burned off.

I-20.name: Discovery of superconductivity
I-20.hee1: Some metals, as they are cooled, suddenly lose everything that blocks the flow of electricity.

I-21.name: Ionic theory and electrode potential
I-21.hee1: Electricity flows through salt water because salt splits into plus and minus particles in water.

I-22.name: Catalysts and surface chemistry
I-22.hee1: A catalyst is still there after the reaction, without being used up

I-23.name: Macromolecular theory
I-23.hee1: Inside plastic, tens of thousands of small molecules hold hands to form long chains.

I-24.name: Discovery of oxygen and the theory of combustion
I-24.hee1: Fire burns because the burning thing combines with the oxygen in the air.

I-25.name: Discovery of the electron and the elementary charge
I-25.hee1: Electricity is really made of tiny particles called "electrons", much smaller and lighter than atoms.

I-26.name: Thermionic emission
I-26.hee1: Inside a vacuum tube, electrons fly out of hot glowing metal like steam

I-27.name: Photoelectric effect and the photon
I-27.hee1: Light is a wave, and also grains of energy of a fixed size.

I-28.name: X-ray diffraction and crystal structure analysis
I-28.hee1: Shine X-rays on a crystal, and the invisible arrangement of atoms shows up as a pattern of dots.

I-29.name: Band theory of solids
I-29.hee1: A semiconductor is a material whose electrons sit right at the edge, needing just a little more energy to move.

I-30.name: Noble gas compounds
I-30.hee1: Even xenon, said to "react with nothing", bonds with fluorine and its relatives

I-31.name: Laws of thermal radiation and the energy quantum
I-31.hee1: The color inside a furnace goes from red to dazzling white because as the temperature rises, more light of short wavelengths appears.

I-32.name: Franck-Hertz experiment
I-32.hee1: Atoms accept only exact, fixed amounts of energy.

I-33.name: Tunneling in semiconductors
I-33.hee1: Electrons sometimes slip through a thin wall they should not be able to cross.

I-34.name: Superconducting tunneling and the quantum voltage standard
I-34.hee1: The standard for "1 volt" is made with tiny superconducting devices and the frequency of microwaves

I-35.name: Quantum Hall effect
I-35.hee1: The standard for "1 ohm" of electrical resistance is made with a cooled transistor and a magnet.

I-36.name: Energy-based neural networks
I-36.hee1: AI research uses ideas from the physics of heat and magnets.

I-37.name: Giant magnetoresistance
I-37.hee1: A hard disk read head has stacked films only a few dozen atoms thick.

I-38.name: Van der Waals equation of state
I-38.hee1: A squeezed gas shrinks less than expected because molecules have size too

I-39.name: Chemical equilibrium and chemical thermodynamics
I-39.hee1: Ammonia plants use high pressure because the harder you push, the more the reaction moves toward ammonia.

I-40.name: Radioactivity and transmutation of elements
I-40.hee1: The helium in balloons was made by uranium in underground rocks over hundreds of millions of years.

I-41.name: Chain reaction
I-41.hee1: An explosion happens all at once because one reaction sets off two, then four, and so on.

I-42.name: Characteristic X-rays and Moseley's law
I-42.hee1: The order of the periodic table is set not by atomic weight but by the electric charge of the nucleus

I-43.name: Fermi–Dirac statistics
I-43.hee1: Like a packed train, electrons can sit only one per seat.

I-44.name: Wave nature of electrons and electron diffraction
I-44.hee1: Electrons are particles, yet they make diffraction patterns like waves.

I-45.name: Quantum theory of chemical bonds
I-45.hee1: In a silicon crystal, every atom holds hands with its four neighbors using its four hands.

I-46.name: Computational chemistry
I-46.hee1: We can now search for new materials by computer calculation before doing experiments

I-47.name: Quantum dots
I-47.hee1: Even with the same material, just making the grains smaller changes the color of light.

I-48.name: Onsager reciprocal relations
I-48.hee1: Electricity arising from a temperature difference and electricity carrying heat are two sides of the same phenomenon.

I-49.name: The field of artificial intelligence
I-49.hee1: The term "artificial intelligence" was first used in a 1955 proposal for a research workshop.

I-50.name: Moore's law
I-50.hee1: Moore's law is not a law of nature but more like a "promise" the whole industry aimed for

I-51.name: Iron–carbon phase diagram and metallography
I-51.hee1: Polish steel and look at it under a microscope, and you see different patterns depending on how much carbon it has.

I-52.name: Dislocation theory
I-52.hee1: Metals bend because "slips" in the arrangement of atoms in the crystal move little by little.

P-01.name: Crane
P-01.hee1: The stones of Greek temples still have holes and grooves for cranes to grab.

P-02.name: Liquid-fuel rocket
P-02.hee1: The first liquid-fuel rocket flew for only about 2.5 seconds.

P-03.name: Electric car
P-03.hee1: Cars powered by electricity were already running in 1881, before gasoline cars

P-04.name: 3D printer
P-04.hee1: The first paper on 3D printing was written by a Japanese researcher.

P-05.name: 3D printer
P-05.hee1: The 3D printer was born from making a toy with a glue gun.

P-06.name: Your computer
P-06.hee1: The computer in front of you holds inventions from many eras, from the typewriter of 150 years ago to the GPU of 1999.

P-07.name: Monitor
P-07.hee1: Screen colors are made only by mixing the brightness of red, green and blue dots

P-08.name: Mouse
P-08.hee1: The first mouse was a wooden box with two wheels.

P-09.name: Keyboard
P-09.hee1: The key layout is still that of typewriters from 150 years ago.

P-10.name: Cooling
P-10.hee1: Without cooling, a computer's chip would reach a dangerous temperature in a few seconds.

P-11.name: Power supply unit
P-11.hee1: A power supply box is small because it switches the electricity on and off tens of thousands of times a second

P-12.name: CPU
P-12.hee1: Today's CPUs have millions of times more transistors than the 4004.

P-13.name: GPU
P-13.hee1: The shadows and light on Minecraft blocks are calculated at the same time by thousands of calculators in the GPU.

P-14.name: Memory
P-14.hee1: Memory rewrites itself dozens of times a second so it does not forget.

P-15.name: SSD
P-15.hee1: Your Minecraft world save is remembered by electrons trapped inside an SSD

P-16.name: Smartphone screen
P-16.hee1: A smartphone screen is a sandwich of many layers: glass, invisible electrodes, and the display.

P-17.name: Smartphone camera
P-17.hee1: A smartphone camera and the eye of an optical mouse are the same kind of chip.

P-18.name: Motion sensor
P-18.hee1: The screen turns when you tip your smartphone sideways because a tiny weight inside moves.

P-19.name: Vibration motor
P-19.hee1: The buzz in silent mode is an off-center weight spinning inside

P-20.name: Smartphone speaker
P-20.hee1: Even the tiny speaker in a smartphone has a strong neodymium magnet inside.

P-21.name: Radio chips and antennas
P-21.hee1: A smartphone's GPS only "listens" to radio waves; it sends nothing to the satellites.

P-22.name: Battery
P-22.hee1: In a smartphone battery, lithium moves in and out of the gaps in graphite.

P-23.name: Memory chip
P-23.hee1: Photos on your phone are remembered by the number of electrons trapped inside a chip

P-24.name: Humanoid robot
P-24.hee1: The humanoid robot built at Waseda University in 1973 could not only walk but also speak simple Japanese.

P-25.name: Robot arm
P-25.hee1: The first factory robot arm was moved not by electric motors but by oil pressure.

P-26.name: Self-driving car
P-26.hee1: The car that won the 2005 driverless car race finished the desert course in about 7 hours with no one aboard.

P-27.name: Digital camera
P-27.hee1: The first digital camera prototype (1975) recorded pictures on a cassette tape

P-28.name: Microphone
P-28.hee1: A karaoke microphone works the same way as a speaker used in reverse.

P-29.name: Air conditioner
P-29.hee1: An air conditioner does not make cold; it carries the room's heat outside.

P-30.name: Refrigerator
P-30.hee1: A refrigerator dumps the heat from inside out into the room from its back and sides (that is why the back of a fridge is warm).

P-31.name: Coffee machine
P-31.hee1: Espresso is made by forcing hot water through coffee grounds at about 9 atmospheres, about 4 times the air pressure in a tire.

P-32.name: Robot vacuum
P-32.hee1: Early Roombas had no map of the room; they cleaned the whole floor just by bumping into things and changing direction, again and again.

P-33.name: Tower fan
P-33.hee1: A bladeless fan really has blades inside its base, and the air from the ring pulls the surrounding air along, multiplying the flow many times.

P-34.name: Elevator
P-34.hee1: Otis did not invent the elevator; what Otis made was a catch mechanism that keeps it from falling even if the rope breaks.

P-35.name: Escalator
P-35.hee1: The first escalator was an amusement park ride, a slanted moving belt instead of stairs.

P-36.name: Automatic door
P-36.hee1: The automatic sliding door was born in a town where strong winds quickly broke swinging doors.

P-37.name: City bus
P-37.hee1: A turbo uses the force of exhaust gas that would have been thrown away to push air into the engine.
